rights_block.jp_public_domain_basis: 日本の著作権保護期間は、2018年末のTPP11整備法による70年化以前は死後50年だった(1970年法改正)。太宰の没後50年=1998年末で日本の保護は満了しており、2018年末の70年化はこの1999〜2018年に既に切れていた作品には遡及しない。太宰の作品は1999-01-01付けで日本において確定的にパブリックドメイン(FICTION-FAMILY-Z-RIGHTS-RECHECK-01_REPORT.md §1、en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_law_of_Japan、確認2026-09-26、HTTP 200)。Aozora Bunkoが全文ダウンロードファイルを公開していることも、著作権消滅済み作品のみをホストするAozoraの運用方針と整合する。
rights_block.us_copyright_status_record_only: 記録事項(必須条件ではない、日本国内向けサービスのため)。走れメロス(1940年発表)は1996-01-01時点で日本において保護期間中だったため、URAA(Uruguay Round Agreements Act)により米国著作権が回復し、発行日から95年=2035年末まで米国で保護される可能性が高い(2036年に米国PD化する可能性が高い)。Cornell University Library "Copyright Term and the Public Domain in the United States" チャート(https://copyright.cornell.edu/publicdomain、確認2026-09-26、HTTP 200)に基づく判定。最終的な法的判断ではない(recon_family_z_production_e2e_01.md §1参照)。
rights_block.legal_use_basis: ユーザー正式決定(2026-09-26、FICTION-FAMILY-Z-RIGHTS-RECHECK-01_REPORT.md §6): 「日本人向け・日本国内向けサービスであるため、Family Zの権利条件は以下で正式採用: (1)日本国内でPublic Domain、または日本国内で適法に利用可能であることを必須条件とする (2)米国PDは必須条件にしない (3)海外向け配信・提供を将来行う場合のみ、その対象法域のrights確認を追加する (4)原作がPDでも、現代の第三者翻訳・英訳・挿絵等は別著作物として扱い、権利未確認のものは流用しない (5)Family Zのadaptationは、確認済み原文/正式Seedから自前生成する。走れメロスは日本でPD確認済みのため初回Family Z E2E対象として継続、差し替え不要。本rights方針はAPPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION。」

known_gap: FAMILY_Z_SEGMENT_ID_GAP(known, recon §6/§8-1 既知課題): 本Storyは8segment(narrator=5件 positions=[1, 3, 5, 7, 8], dialogue_voice=3件 positions=[2, 4, 6])に分割されるが、er020_tts_retry_local_rewrite_01.resolve_narrative_role()は"full_story_part1/2/3"の3スロットの完全一致文字列しかFULL_STORYロールとして認識しない。position 4以降(narrator/dialogue voice問わず)はConnected Speechの適用対象外のまま(raw_segment_idのまま)であり、これは新しい設計判断ではなくresolve_narrative_role()の既存の完全一致判定をread-only参照した結果そのままの事実。resolver側にFamily Z用パターンを追加するか(recon §8-2選択肢(b))、Family Z側のsegment_id命名を作り直すか(選択肢(a))は本委任のスコープ外の判断であり、Fable/ユーザー判断を要する。
mapping_caveat_voice_mismatch: CAVEAT: proposed_segment_id(full_story_part1/2/3)はposition1〜3に機械的・位置基準で割り当てただけであり、voice(誰が話すか)は考慮していない。今回のrunでは position=[2]がnarratorではなくdialogue voice(短い引用符区間)であり、'Full Story narration'という本来のFULL_STORYロールの意味とは厳密にはズレる。これは新しい判断ではなく、事実の記録(このrunの実際の分割結果)であり、Fable/ユーザー判断を要する論点としてknown_gapと合わせて報告する。

comment_1.text: 小国の統治者ディオニュシオスは、疑いだけで人を処刑する恐ろしい人です。羊飼いメロスは不正を直接批判し、死刑を宣告されました。妹の結婚式のため三日間の猶予を得ましたが、その間、友人セリヌンティウスが人質として残ります。

in_one_line.text: Melos kept his promise, and his loyalty saved his friend. The ruler learned that trust and justice are stronger than fear.
in_one_line.prompt:
You are writing the closing "In One Line" summary for a short English-learner audio story (A2 level, a Public Domain literature adaptation). Write 1-2 sentences in English that capture what the story's ending means, in the same spirit as a closing remark after a short story. Do not introduce new facts that are not in the story. Do not use meta-narration phrases like "Let's listen" or "What do you think happens next?".

[Full story text, for reference only, do not add new facts]
In a small kingdom, the ruler, Dionysius, was afraid of enemies. If anyone spoke against him, his guards could take that person to prison. Often, the ruler ordered executions without a fair trial.

One day, a shepherd named Melos stood before him.

“You punish people before you know the truth,” Melos said. “That is not justice.”

The ruler’s face became hard. “Then you will die.”

Melos’s sister was going to be married in three days. He fell to his knees.

“Please let me go to her wedding,” he said. “I will return before my death.”

The ruler laughed. “Why should I believe you?”

Melos’s friend, Selinuntius, stepped forward. “I will stay here in his place.”

So the ruler agreed. Melos had three days to go and return. If he did not come back, his friend would die.

Melos ran from the city. He reached the river, but heavy rain had made the water wild. The small boat broke against a rock. Melos fell into the cold river and nearly disappeared under the water. At last, he reached the other side, shaking and weak.

He hurried to the wedding. He smiled for his sister, but his eyes stayed on the road. When the wedding ended, he left at once.

On the way back, three attackers jumped from behind some trees. They took his horse and pushed him to the ground. Melos tried to stand, but pain filled his body. He walked through the night, then fell beside the road.

The sky was becoming bright. The time was almost finished.

Melos looked toward the city. “I cannot do this,” he whispered. “Perhaps my friend is already dead.”

For a moment, he wanted to hide in the forest.

Then he remembered his friend’s calm face. His friend had trusted him enough to face death.

“No,” Melos said. “I gave my word.”

He stood and ran.

At the city gate, the guards were leading his friend to the place of execution. Then Melos shouted, “Wait!”

Everyone turned. Melos fell before the ruler.

“I promised to return,” he said. “I am here.”

The ruler looked at the two friends. Slowly, he lowered his hand.

“Free him,” he said.

After that day, the ruler demanded fair trials. He had learned that trust and loyalty could be stronger than fear.
